arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Miller argued the employer is liable when a supervisor uses delegated authority to cause harm.
Mr. Davis argued the parties agree Linda Buck made the final decision to fire Staub.
Mr. Davis argued there is no evidence Linda Buck possessed animus toward Staub.
Mr. Schnapper argued agency law determines the employer's responsibility for specific officials.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether an employer faces liability when a biased supervisor influences a neutral decisionmaker. The lower court ruled against Staub. It required the supervisor to exert singular influence over the final decision.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Staub wants the Court to hold the employer liable for the supervisor's biased report.
Proctor Hospital wants the Court to limit liability to the neutral decisionmaker's own motives.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Staub argues agency law makes the employer responsible for the supervisor's discriminatory actions.
Proctor Hospital argues the statute only covers actions by the official with discharge authority.
